newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts' comments on Dutch PTT split.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comments on Dutch PTT split.

text.p: PTT Nederland NV said on Tuesday it would split itself into separate post and telecommunications units and it would possibly seek separate bourse listing for the two businesses.
Following is a selection of analysts comments.

"The news has come sooner than the market had expected. KPN said two weeks ago it would decide on a possible split towards the end of this year. Also, the division of the two units will become effective relatively soon, even though it will be quite a complicated task. The telecoms unit will be able to better profile itself without the postal arm, which is positive for possible cross-holdings. A split would give investors the opportunity to choose whether they want to invest in post or in telecoms. On the whole, it's a positive thing."

"It's not a major surprise, but it's a positive step. It all but guarantees a separate listing for PTT post in 1998. I'd expect the demerger to add modest value to the group giving greater focus to the attractions of PTT post which is likely to achieve a greater multiple than KPN currently stands on. European investors tend to like restructuring stories and this is one of them."

"The surprise is that they haven't announced an outright separate listing which would make more sense to me. It would give investors more clarity, making comparisons for the telecoms unit easier. It would increase the telecoms international opportunities, whereas the postal arm in itself is a healthy company with good growth possibilities outside Europe. I think the market reaction is somewhat exaggerated given the separate listing isn't sure. The main advantage of a split would be to investors; on an operational level, (the units) are pretty well separated already."
